newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on weather, import talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on weather, import talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Monday, hit by forecasts for nearly ideal growing weather and renewed talk that U.S. firms were importing South American supplies, pit sources said.
Nearbys collapsed late on profit taking and on unwinding of July/Nov spreads, but July was underpinned by concerns of tight supplies and by USDA weekly export sales figures.
"The soycomplex is torn between a tight cash situation and the prospects for a bumper, record crop," said John Kleist, director of agricultural research for ING Futures and Options in Chicago.
Forecasts called for showers across much of the U.S. Midwest, followed by warmer weather, meteorologists said. Floor sources said that forecast was a nearly ideal recipe for good crop development.

Talk again surfaced that U.S. firms would import Brazilian soybeans after basis levels there cracked on Friday, making it even more profitable to import soybeans. Meanwhile, Brazilian traders said Cargill Inc was loading Brazilian soybeans destined for southern Georgia. Shipment was set for June 20.
Soybean futures ended 17 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower with July down 16 at $8.38-1/2.

The July contract was underpinned much of the session by USDA weekly export sales which came in above trade expectation. USDA put inspections at 9.187 million bushels. The trade had expected four million to seven million bushels.

But nearbys collapsed late on unwinding of bull spreads and outright selling, led by E.D. and F. Man International, pit sources said. Traders said Man sold three million bushels July in the waning minutes of trade.
On the day, Refco Inc sold five million bushels November, one million August and 1.5 million July. Cargill bought two million November and one million each July and August.
Lind-Waldock spread two million bushels November/August at $1.13, premium August, and Prudential Securities spread two million August/September at 76 to 77 cents, premium August.
In options trade, Rosenthal Collins sold 600 July $8.75 calls at 3-1/4 to 2-3/4 cents and bought 600 July $9.00 calls at 1-1/4 cents.
Continental Grain sold 200 November $6.75 puts at 42 cents, pit sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 58,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 77,336 contracts.
